skill.name: azure-speech-to-text-rest-py
skill.description: Use Azure Speech to Text REST API examples to transcribe short audio files with Python, without the Speech SDK.
skill.summary: Transcribe short audio with Azure Speech REST calls in Python.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static detections for Markdown backticks, Azure URLs, environment variables, and API keys are mostly safe documentation patterns for the stated Azure Speech workflow. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found. One medium semantic issue remains because region values are interpolated into request URLs without validation.

remediation.issue: Region values are interpolated into Azure request URLs without validation.
remediation.suggestion: Validate the region against an Azure region allow-list or use a trusted full endpoint before sending keys or audio.

remediation.issue: The examples send audio content to Azure Speech but provide limited privacy guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear note that audio leaves the local environment and may require user consent or data handling review.

remediation.issue: HTTP request examples omit production timeout and retry controls.
remediation.suggestion: Add request timeouts, bounded retries, and failure logging guidance for production integrations.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Region Used in Service URLs
semantic_findings.description: The examples interpolate AZURE_SPEECH_REGION directly into request URLs before sending audio and credentials. A malicious or malformed region value could redirect requests away from Azure.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The URL host is built from an environment value in several examples, and the same flow sends the subscription key or audio. This is a realistic misconfiguration risk, although the documented intended value is an Azure region.

content.user_title: Transcribe Short Audio with Azure Speech
content.value_statement: Short audio transcription needs reliable REST examples without SDK setup. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Azure Speech requests.
actual_capabilities: Shows Python requests examples for Azure Speech short audio REST calls.
Demonstrates subscription key and bearer token authentication patterns.
Covers WAV PCM and OGG OPUS content-type headers.
Provides chunked transfer and async aiohttp transcription examples.
Explains response formats, recognition statuses, profanity options, and language codes.
Identifies when to use the Speech SDK or Batch Transcription instead.
limitations: Only covers short audio up to 60 seconds.
Requires a user-owned Azure Speech resource and credentials.
Does not cover real-time streaming, batch transcription, translation, or custom models.
Production code still needs validation, timeouts, retries, and privacy review.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Transcription Feature
use_cases.description: Add a simple REST transcription path for short WAV or OGG files.

use_cases.title: Document Azure Speech Integration
use_cases.description: Create internal guidance for environment variables, headers, and response handling.

use_cases.title: Validate Language and Audio Choices
use_cases.description: Check language codes, content types, and endpoint limits before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Start a REST Call
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the smallest Python request for Azure Speech short audio using my region and key environment variables.

prompt_templates.title: Set Audio Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose headers and query parameters for a WAV file in Spanish using detailed output.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Design error handling for Azure Speech REST responses, including authentication and recognition status cases.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Use
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure Speech transcription workflow for production risks, including secrets, timeouts, retries, and audio privacy.

output_examples.input: Transcribe an English WAV file with detailed output.
output: Use the conversation recognition REST endpoint.
Set the language to en-US and request detailed output.
Return display text, recognition status, and confidence information.

output_examples.input: Use bearer token authentication instead of a subscription key header.
output: Request a short-lived token from the Azure token endpoint.
Send the token as a bearer authorization header.
Cache the token for less than its ten minute lifetime.

output_examples.input: Decide whether this API fits a 20 minute recording.
output: This endpoint does not fit long recordings.
Use Batch Transcription or the Speech SDK instead.

best_practices: Store Azure Speech keys in environment variables or a secret manager.
Validate region and language values before building request URLs.
Use short WAV PCM 16 kHz mono files and handle every recognition status.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding subscription keys in prompts, scripts, or shared files.
Sending long recordings or streaming use cases through the short audio endpoint.
Trusting transcript text without checking recognition status and confidence.

faq.question: Does this skill require the Azure Speech SDK?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on REST API calls using Python HTTP libraries.

faq.question: What audio length does it support?
faq.answer: It covers short audio up to 60 seconds. Pronunciation assessment is limited to 30 seconds.

faq.question: Can it transcribe live audio streams?
faq.answer: No. Use the Speech SDK when you need real-time streaming or interim results.

faq.question: Where should I store Azure credentials?
faq.answer: Use environment variables or a managed secret store. Do not paste keys into prompts or files.

faq.question: Can it return confidence scores?
faq.answer: Yes. Request detailed output to receive alternatives and confidence information.

faq.question: Does audio leave my environment?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples send audio to Azure Speech. Review privacy and compliance requirements first.
